claim.why_it_matters: Same merge defect as Format 2: the ASCENDING/DESCENDING brace spans both lines, encloses 'DYNAMIC [' as an alternative (splitting the CAPACITY bracket across the brace boundary), KEY is moved to the top line, and the brace opens outside its bracket. The figure thereby makes DYNAMIC an alternative to ASCENDING/DESCENDING and leaves the [ CAPACITY ... ] bracket opened inside the brace and closed outside it.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 370 (printed 346) at 300 dpi. Format 4 prints line 1 as plain text: 'OCCURS DYNAMIC [ CAPACITY IN data-name-3 ] [FROM integer-4 ] [ TO integer-5 ] [ INITIALIZED ]', with no brace. Line 2 is a bracket that encloses a brace around stacked ASCENDING/DESCENDING, followed by 'KEY IS { data-name-2 } ...', then the closing bracket, then '... [ INDEXED BY { index-name-1 } ... ]'. Format 1 on the same page is transcribed correctly in exactly that shape. In the transcription the brace runs over both lines and contains 'DYNAMIC [' as an alternative. KEY is detached to the top line, and the bracket's left edge sits outside the brace. Read under §2014:5.2.5.2, the transcribed figure makes DYNAMIC a brace alternative to ASCENDING/DESCENDING and splits the CAPACITY bracket. That changes the syntax, so it is a normative defect. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
